title: The adjugate identity for a square matrix
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$ an integer and $M$ an $m\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. Let $\operatorname{adj}(M)$ be its adjugate, the $m\times m$ matrix whose $(i,j)$ entry is $(-1)^{i+j}\det(M^{(j,i)})$, where $M^{(j,i)}$ is the $(m-1)\times(m-1)$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] of $M$ obtained by deleting row $j$ and column $i$ (the transpose of the cofactor matrix; for $m=0$ it is the empty matrix). Then $\operatorname{adj}(M)\,M=M\,\operatorname{adj}(M)=\det(M)\cdot1_{m\times m}$.
